newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil plans to grant TV, radio concessions again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil plans to grant TV, radio concessions again.

text.p: Brazil later this year plans to grant new television and radio concessions for the first time since the late 1980s, an official for the Communications Ministry said.

Ministry spokesman Francisco Mendonca said the government this month will begin auctioning off 610 new licenses but decisions on who gets the licenses would not be made until after municipal elections early in October.
"This is to avoid any suggestion or rumors that concessions are being awarded politically," he said.
Mendonca added he did not know how many would be for TV and how many for radio. But O Estado de S. Paulo newspaper reported Monday that 60 TV, 400 FM radio and 150 AM licenses would be granted.
The licenses would be the first granted by Brazil since the government of former president Jose Sarney, whose five-year term ended in 1990, he said.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's government decided to once again grant concessions after rewriting the rules governing the awarding of radio and TV licenses last November, he added.
"The government eliminated a provision allowing for personal criteria in awarding concessions and replaced it with competitive criteria to make it more democratic, pluralistic," Mendonca said.
Some 40 percent of Brazil's 2,944 radio stations are directly or indirectly controlled by politicians while 27 percent of its 257 TV operators are politicians.
